text: U.S. stock indices declined sharply on Thursday, with the Nasdaq Composite leading the losses as investors reacted to concerns over surging artificial intelligence capital expenditures and escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The selloff was broad-based, pressured by rising oil prices and higher Treasury yields, while the technology sector lagged due to disappointing earnings and heavy spending forecasts from major companies like Alphabet and Tesla. Conversely, memory stocks showed relative resilience, edging higher against the broader market trend.
